title: platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026
author: Diego Alvarez
summary: Platform team wiki index and runbook collection. Includes how-tos, dashboards, alert standards, onboarding checklist, and retrospective templates for platform systems and services.
body:
Overview
This page is the canonical index for the Platform team wiki and runbook collection at Redwood Inference. It consolidates operational how-tos, dashboard standards, alerting conventions, runbook templates, and onboarding resources. The audience is Platform engineers, SREs, and new hires who will operate or contribute runbooks and service docs.

1. Wiki Structure and Navigation
- Home: platform team wiki landing page with links to oncall, runbooks, capacity plans, and roadmap.
- Runbooks: directory that contains per-service runbooks using the standard template.
- How-tos: operational recipes for common tasks (deployments, scaling, adding alerts, tracing).
- Dashboards: dashboard catalog with ownership metadata and recommended panels.
- Roadmap & Retrospectives: quarterly roadmap entries and postmortem summaries.
- Node catalog & instance types: hardware profiles and recommended use cases for each node type.

2. Runbook Template (must be copied for each service)
- Title: short service name + incident scenario
- Owner: primary and secondary oncall owners
- Pager duty: escalation policy and links
- SLOs: expressed as numbers (uptime, p99 latency, error budget)
- Symptoms: what you will observe in dashboards and logs
- Immediate mitigations: steps to reduce impact (3 bullet max for first responder)
- Investigation checklist: queries, traces, log file locations, and known failure modes
- Recovery steps: commands, config changes, and rollback instructions
- Verification: metrics to confirm recovery and required observation window
- Post-incident actions: required follow-ups and owners
- Last reviewed: date and reviewer names

3. Dashboards: Required Panels and Naming Conventions
- All dashboards live in Grafana under the folder: Platform/<service-name>.
- Required panels for each service: request rate, error rate, latency p50/p90/p99, successful responses, deployment version, CPU/memory, queue depth.
- Naming convention: platform.<service>.<panel-description> (e.g., platform.control-plane-api.p99-latency).
- Ownership: every dashboard must list an owner and a Slack contact in the dashboard description.

4. Alerts: Standard Alerts and Annotations
- Alert tiers: PAGER (P0/P1), OPS (P2), INFO (P3).
- Example alert queries and thresholds:
  - PAGER: platform.<service>.high-error-rate -> http_errors_5m > 1.5% for 5m AND request_rate > 5rps
  - PAGER: platform.<service>.p99-high -> p99_latency > 2s for 5m
  - OPS: platform.<service>.cpu-high -> cpu_utilization > 90% for 10m
  - INFO: platform.<service>.cache-low -> cache_hit_rate < 60% for 30m
- Alert annotations (required): owner, runbook_url, sla_impact, runbook_last_reviewed

5. How-tos (operational recipes)
- Create a runbook entry:
  1) Duplicate the runbook template page and fill in owner, SLOs, and links to dashboards.
  2) Add runbook_url to relevant alert annotations.
  3) Tag the page with labels: service:<name>, runbook, oncall.
- Add a new Grafana alert rule:
  1) Create or duplicate rule in Grafana/Alertmanager.
  2) Add annotations owner and runbook_url.
  3) Ensure paging channel is Platform-Oncall and update PagerDuty mapping.
- Deploy a canary in k8s:
  1) Apply canary manifest with traffic-slice label and annotate canary owner.
  2) Monitor the Deployment Canary dashboard for 30 minutes.
  3) If stable, increment traffic slices and promote; else rollback with kubectl rollout undo.

6. Onboarding Checklist for Platform New Hires
- Day 0: Account access, Slack, Zoom, and corp VPN.
- Day 1-7: Complete security training and obtain least-privilege kube credentials.
- Day 7-14: Shadow oncall, review two runbooks, and run through a simulated game-day.
- By day 14: Complete "Platform Oncall 101" checklist and be able to perform a basic rollback and alert modification under supervision.

Checklist items (must be checked in wiki):
- cluster access verified
- pagerduty access verified
- read key runbooks: control-plane-api, routing-service, telemetry-pipeline
- complete canary deployment walkthrough

7. Retrospectives and Postmortems
- Postmortem template fields: summary, impact, timeline, root cause, corrective action, detection and mitigation timeline, action owners, review notes.
- Timebox: postmortem draft within 72 hours, published within 7 days.
- Quarterly retro: platform lead to schedule review of SLO burn and repeat offenders; produce at least one reliability improvement with owner and deadline.

8. Runbook Maintenance and Review Policy
- Every runbook must be reviewed at least once every 6 months. Set runbook_last_reviewed annotation on alerts and dashboard descriptions.
- When a service or SLO changes, update runbook within one sprint and add a changelog entry at the bottom of the runbook.

9. Team Contacts and Ownership
- Platform lead: Priya Singh (priya@redwood.com)
- Observability lead: Noah Patel (noah@redwood.com)
- Platform wiki maintainers: Diego Alvarez, Sophie Kim
- Oncall Slack channel: #oncall-platform

10. Useful Commands and Queries
- Create incident channel: /incident start platform --title "<short description>" --severity P1
- Add incident note: incident-note add "<text>"
- PromQL examples:
  - error_rate_5m: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\",service=~\"$service\"}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service=~\"$service\"}[5m])) by (service)
  - p99_latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))

Change log
- 2025-11-12: Created by Diego Alvarez (initial wiki index and runbook template)
- 2025-12-20: Added onboarding checklist and alert annotation requirements (reviewed by Priya Singh)
- 2026-02-20: Updated dashboard naming conventions and runbook review policy (reviewed by Noah Patel)

If you find gaps in this index or missing runbooks, please open a PR against the wiki page or add an item to the platform backlog.
